subject: Short-term audit window & BYOK exception for Acme POC — decision needed
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short-term audit window & BYOK exception for Acme POC — decision needed

Team — forwarding a request from Acme Health that landed this morning. TL;DR: they want a 7-day audit-log retention window (shorter than our default), and they want to run a POC that uses their own KMS keys (BYOK) with a short-lived exception to our standard escrow/rotation policy while procurement completes. They also asked about SSO session token retention (they need tokens trimmed to 4 hours for the POC).

Key context (attached mapping): acme-poc-mapping.xlsx. Their compliance lead (Sarah) says this is a timeboxed POC for a pilot contract; procurement wants the procurement-term-sheet.pdf signed within three weeks. They flagged audits@thirdpartysecurity.io as an independent reviewer who will ask for evidence exports.

Questions we need to resolve internally before replying to Acme: 
- Can Security accept a temporary BYOK mode without full escrow for a timeboxed POC? What minimum evidence/controls do we need to provide?
- Product: what implementation effort is required to allow a short-term per-tenant retention window override (7 days) and a SSO session override to 4 hours? Risk to platform and roadmap slot?
- Ops: if we permit a temporary key rotation exemption, what are the operational steps (manual verification, audit of rotation events)?

Proposed quick cadence: Decision by end of day Monday 5/11 so we can confirm the POC kickoff on 5/18. I put an initial proposal in the attached sso-retention-matrix.pdf. Please reply with blockers/requirements and owner for the customer response.

Thanks —
Ben
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0142

Attachments: acme-poc-mapping.xlsx, sso-retention-matrix.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term audit window & BYOK exception for Acme POC — decision needed

Ben — thanks for the summary. Quick product read:

- Short-term retention override (7 days) is feasible via the existing retention-config flag per-tenant. We have a guarded path already for ephemeral pilots, but it requires a manual approval and a config change in prod that currently needs an eng oncall + product owner signoff. Rough ETA: 2-3 days of coordination (non-cumulative work).
- SSO token window to 4 hours is a config toggle in the auth layer, but we must ensure session revocation hooks are in place; otherwise tokens will remain valid on cached clients. Testing matrix: we need to validate revocation propagation (1 day).
- BYOK: supporting customer's KMS key is more involved. Currently we support customer-managed keys for storage at rest, but onboarding a new external KMS with shortened escrow is a compliance question. From a product perspective we can gate the POC behind: 1) an explicit manual opt-in, 2) a timeframe (7 days), and 3) logging/visibility into any failed key rotations. Implementation effort for a safe short-term flow: ~5 engineering days + security review.

Recommend this approach for the reply to Acme: we offer a timeboxed POC with three conditions — manual approval, explicit acceptance of limited evidence export (logs + KMS rotation audit only), and a rollback plan. I'll volunteer to own the product checklist and test plan if we get signoff.

On the legal/commercial side, cc'ing @Grace to flag any procurement language we should insist on.

Subject: Re: Short-term audit window & BYOK exception for Acme POC — decision needed

Thanks — copying Security perspective. Short answers up front: possible, but with concrete controls and evidence. Longer: 

1) BYOK without escrow for a POC is high risk if we lose visibility into key lifecycle. If Acme insists on withholding escrow, we require at minimum:
   - A signed timeboxed attestation that keys will not be rotated during the window OR a rotation log delivered on every rotation event (timestamped, signed).
   - An automated export of KMS access logs to our audit bucket (read-only) for the POC window.

2) Audit logs: 7-day retention by request is ok provided we keep a write-once copy internally for dispute windows — we can implement a short-term retention flag but it must create an immutable snapshot (S3 WriteOnce/GOVERNANCE object lock) accessible only to security for 90 days. That keeps us safe legally while still meeting their short-term visibility need.

3) SSO tokens: 4-hour session is acceptable, but we must enforce immediate revocation on role/permission changes. Product must wire up a forced session revocation API call in the POC.

4) Evidence exports: thirdparty reviewer will want chain-of-custody. We should provide a signed manifest for each export (sha256 sums, timestamp, and responsible operator).

Operational asks: one security engineer must be on the POC change window for the duration. If we accept this flow, we'll need to open an 'exception' ticket in our compliance tracker (JIRA-REQ-9021) with the terms: start/end dates, owners, and rollback triggers.

I'll volunteer to be security owner for the exception but need legal signoff on the attestation language.

From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, audits@thirdpartysecurity.io
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term audit window & BYOK exception for Acme POC — decision needed

Ben — appreciate the quick internal loop. We're operating under a tight compliance window for the POC: clinical team wants to start 5/18 and procurement will only sign earlier if we can demonstrate controls for the pilot. We're ok with a timeboxed exception if Redwood provides:

- A written attestation about key-handling during the POC window (we expect no unexpected rotations)
- Access to audit-log exports for the POC period (we will sign an NDA for the export handling)
- A 4-hour SSO token policy for users involved in the pilot

I've attached the procurement-term-sheet.pdf (redacted). We can accept the immutable internal snapshot approach you suggested if it helps move things forward. Please let me know by Monday EOD if Redwood can commit.

Thanks —
Sarah Jones
Compliance Lead, Acme Health
sarah.jones@acmehealth.com
+1 617-555-0188

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 16:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term audit window & BYOK exception for Acme POC — decision needed

Update and decision: after reviewing risk and product effort, we can accommodate Acme's request for a timeboxed POC with the following firm conditions — please treat this as the customer's formal reply draft.

Agreed exception terms (start: 2026-05-18, end: 2026-05-24):
- BYOK: Acme may use customer-managed keys for the POC. Acme must sign an attestation that keys will not be rotated during the POC window OR provide signed rotation logs if rotations occur. Acme will grant read-only export of KMS access logs to our audit bucket for the window.
- Audit logs: Redwood will apply a 7-day retention override for the Acme tenant for the POC window and will create an immutable snapshot retained internally for 90 days for dispute resolution.
- SSO: Redwood will set session token TTL to 4 hours for pilot users and enforce immediate revocation hooks on role changes.
- Evidence/external review: any export to audits@thirdpartysecurity.io must include a signed manifest (sha256 + timestamp + operator).

Owners & next steps:
- Product/POC checklist: Marissa Cole — own test plan and coordinate config changes (ETA: 3 days).
- Security owner: Jonas Weber — prepare attestation language and be on-call for the POC window.
- Legal/Commercial: Grace O'Connor — review procurement-term-sheet.pdf and signoff on attestation wording.
- Sales/Customer liaison: Ben Carter — confirm dates with Acme and track procurement acceptance.

Operational notes: this requires a manual approval ticket (JIRA-REQ-9021) and an eng oncall change window to flip the per-tenant flags. Marissa, please create the ticket and include rollback steps. Jonas, please prepare the snapshot process (S3 governance lock) and export manifest template.
